plainTranslation: A's mind meets B's mind. The opposition pulls them into push-and-pull.
policy: Governed by synastry-policy. Descriptive, not deterministic; intensity is never treated as obligation, safety concerns override astrology.

summaryDeep:
This person may hear the side of the story you did not lead with. They may ask the question you were trying to move past. They may slow you down when you want to get to the point, or push the conversation forward when you are still sorting through the details.

This can be irritating. It can also be useful.

One of you may speak to understand. The other may need time before words feel honest. One of you may want facts. The other may hear the emotional truth underneath the facts. One of you may look at the pattern. The other may stay with the specific thing that happened.

When this works, the difference gives the relationship range. You stop mistaking your first thought for the whole truth. This person can help you see what you missed. You can help them name what they are circling around. Together, you can build a fuller picture than either mind could build alone.

The challenge comes when the conversation becomes more focused on proving a point than understanding each other. One person explains, the other responds, and before long both of you are reacting instead of listening. Each person is working so hard to be understood that genuine understanding starts to disappear from the exchange.

The practice is simple, but it takes intention. Slow down enough to hear what they are actually saying instead of rushing toward your rebuttal. Get curious about the perspective behind their words. You do not have to agree with their conclusions to learn from them. Sometimes the very thing that frustrates you is the thing expanding your view. Respect the possibility that their mind is holding a piece of the truth that is harder for you to see from your side of the conversation.
